$comment: Roofs as props (tools/content/kit/academy.mjs spireMesh; docs/map-briefs/st_johns, step 3): a turret's conical roof, shingled, with a finial, to cap a round turret (setpiece.corner_turret_round's cone tops) or any round tower. Round in plan, it fills its box; it collides as three stacked boxes, a stepped cone.

notes.1: First version: a shingled cone 3.4 m across at its eaves and 4.6 m to the finial's tip (3.7 m of cone), nine courses of shingles over a short skirt, a rod, ball and spike for a finial; variants slate and red shingle. Collides as three stacked boxes.

First version (St. John's step 10, photos 2 and 3: the gym's barrel vault on steel trusses): one 8 m bay of a barrel-vaulted roof 24 m across: the boarded underside rising 2.3 m from springing to crown with a sheet roof over it (so a hall left open at the top is roofed by it), a steel bowstring truss across the bay's middle, four pendant lamp shades hung from its tie (looks only: a set piece's light gives the light). Its springing is 1.6 m over its foot: place the foot 1.6 m under the walls' top. Variant end fills the vault's end on -z (the gable over a hall's end wall). Collides as nothing.

First version (St. John's step 7d, the mess hall's pieces; OWNER_NOTES_2026-11-21): one 8 m bay of a timber ceiling for a hall 16 m across: heavy beams across the hall on stone corbels at its middle and its ends (half of an end's beam is the next bay's), joists along it every 0.8 m, boards over them facing down. 0.7 m from the corbels' foot to the boards: place its foot 0.7 m under the ceiling. Collides as nothing.

First version (St. John's step 8b, the library's roof as the owner's photo shows it): a steep eight-sided pyramid of weathered brown-red shingles 17.4 m across the flats of its flared eave and 15 m to the point of its small copper cap, for a faceted (octagonal) hall end or tower 16 m across with a 0.7 m overhang. Drawn inside too (pale panels, dark rafters). Variant `hall` is cut away on −z where it would hang inside a Ridge Roof Bay running off that way (ridge 5.6 m over the eaves): place both at the walls' top and the two roofs are one room inside. Collides as nothing.

First version (St. John's step 8b; the owner's interior photo: an open timber roof on arch-braced trusses, close rafters against pale panels): one 8 m bay of a ridge roof over a hall 16 m across: brown-red shingle slopes with a flared eave 0.7 m outside the walls, the ridge 5.6 m over the eaves; underneath pale panels, twelve rafters a slope, purlins and a ridge beam, and two arch-braced trusses (wall posts on stone corbels 1.5 m down the wall, principals, a collar, curved braces, a king post). Its eaves are 1.8 m over its foot: place the foot 1.8 m under the walls' top. Variant `end` closes the gable on −z with a wall (the hall's end). Collides as nothing.
notes.2: The gable's verge closed (St. John's Memorial Hall pass, owner 2026-11-23: "the roofline edges look strange; you can almost see through them"): the slopes were a skin with open ends and the gable wall stopped 6 cm under the shingles, so a slit ran from eave to ridge along every gable; a dark barge board 0.45 m deep now runs up each slope at the gable's face, 3 cm over the shingles and 2 cm proud. Variant `one_truss`: a single truss in the bay's middle, so a hall's upper windows can stand either side of it, clear of its post and corbel (St. John's Memorial Hall, Rounded corners).
notes.3: The eave's hollow closed from below (owner, 2026-11-24, St. John's: a sloped timber attic showed sky along both wall tops): the soffit stopped at the wall's outer face and the wall plate stood at the inner face of a 0.5 m wall, so over a thinner wall (the Gable Annex's 0.3 m) the hollow between the flared eave and the soffit was open to the room and the sky showed through the shingles' backs. A dark underside now runs from the plate's foot out to the soffit, so the roof is closed whatever the wall's thickness. The gable wall's foot is closed too (between its two faces: over the annex's 0.3 m front wall a strip of sky showed along the wall's top).

notes.1: First version (St. John's step 8b; the owner's photo: the library's small stucco wing under a steep roof with a swept, kicked-out eave and a little half-timber in its gable): a ridge roof 6 m long over a wing 5 m across (6.2 m over its swept eaves), the ridge 3.5 m over the eaves, a half-timbered gable wall on +z; its −z end is open (it goes against a taller building's wall); panels inside, no trusses. Place its foot on the walls' top. Variant `plain`: a boarded gable. Collides as nothing.
notes.2: The gable's verge closed (St. John's Memorial Hall pass, owner 2026-11-23: "the roofline edges look strange; you can almost see through them"): the slopes were a skin with open ends and the gable wall stopped 6 cm under the shingles, so a slit ran from eave to ridge along every gable; a dark barge board 0.45 m deep now runs up each slope at the gable's face, 3 cm over the shingles and 2 cm proud.
notes.3: The eave's hollow closed from below (owner, 2026-11-24, St. John's: a sloped timber attic showed sky along both wall tops): the soffit stopped at the wall's outer face and the wall plate stood at the inner face of a 0.5 m wall, so over a thinner wall (the Gable Annex's 0.3 m) the hollow between the flared eave and the soffit was open to the room and the sky showed through the shingles' backs. A dark underside now runs from the plate's foot out to the soffit, so the roof is closed whatever the wall's thickness. The gable wall's foot is closed too (between its two faces: over the annex's 0.3 m front wall a strip of sky showed along the wall's top).

notes.1: First version (St. John's Memorial Hall pass, owner 2026-11-23: "round all four corners of the hall, with the roof following"): the Faceted Spire's steep shingle pyramid over a square plan with rounded corners (4.7 m of radius at the eave: the walls' 4 m corners and the 0.7 m overhang), each corner a cone between two flat faces, the same flared eave, courses, copper cap and inside (pale panels, dark rafters). 17.4 m across its eave, 15 m to the point. Variant `hall` is cut away on −z where a Ridge Roof Bay runs in under it. Collides as nothing.

First version (St. John's Memorial Hall pass, owner 2026-11-23: "round all four corners of the hall, with the roof following"): a hall's hipped end over rounded corners: the −z half of a shingle pyramid whose point is a Ridge Roof Bay's ridge end at the +z face (same span, rise 5.6 m and flared eave, so the two meet in one line), its corners cones of 4.7 m radius at the eave, its end slope as steep as the sides; panels and rafters inside. 17.4 m across, 5.6 m high, 8.7 m out from the ridge's end. Its foot goes on the walls' top (a Ridge Roof Bay's foot is 1.8 m lower). Collides as nothing.
